title: Mortal guilt needs special confession and sorrow; venial mostly covered by general humble acknowledgment
source_text: XLIV. Deinde, quia ad expurgandum peccatorum mortalium reatum requiritur specialis eorum agnitio & confessio, specialis item dolor & contritio. At pro venia-lium maxima parte expurganda acceptatur generalis, sed humilis, seria, & dolorosa nostrae corruptionis agnitio, adjunctam habens generalem illam deprecationem, Ab occultis munda me. Propterea quod leviora illa & quotidianae incursiones delicta, multo maxima ex parte scientiam nostram fugiunt. Licet ea hujus generis peccata, quae a nobis observantur, speciatim quoque agnoscenda atque deploranda sint.
pass_a_gloss: Next, because for purging the guilt of mortal sins special acknowledgment and confession of them is required, likewise special grief and contrition. But for purging the greatest part of venials a general yet humble, serious, and sorrowful acknowledgment of our corruption is accepted, having joined to it that general prayer, Cleanse me from secret faults. Because those lighter faults and daily-incursion offenses for the most part escape our knowledge. Although sins of this kind which are observed by us ought also to be specially acknowledged and deplored.
pass_b_english: Mortal guilt: name it, confess it, grieve it specially.
Most venials hide from us—so a humble general corruption-plea (‘cleanse me from secret faults’) can cover them, without canceling special sorrow for noticed slips.

choices.why: General humble confession for unseen venials, not indifference.
